title: Phase Slab Allocator: kernel probing + tenant SLA buckets
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Design and implement a 'Phase Slab Allocator' — a granular prefill/decode scheduling policy that groups requests into latency-economy slabs (fast, balanced, economical) and uses lightweight kernel-probing + attention micro-probing to choose optimal kernel variants and microbatch packing strategies per slab. This ticket pairs phase-splitting with tenant SLA buckets and runtime kernel hints to improve p99 latency for latency-sensitive tenants while retaining throughput for economical workloads.

Background: Current runtime uses coarse-grained phase splitters and kernel selection heuristics that are globally applied. We see p99 tail spikes when mixed workloads (short-chat vs long-batched-embeddings) share a node and when attention-dense inputs cause kernel slowdowns. Existing tickets have explored admission controllers and congestion control, but we need a runtime policy that can: 1) make per-request slab assignments based on latency budgets and recent tail behavior, 2) probe and cache kernel performance estimates conditioned on attention density and sequence length distribution, 3) allocate microbatches within slabs to respect latency envelopes.

Design proposal:
- Slabs: three runtime slabs: FAST (tight SLAs, low batching, hedged fast kernels), BALANCED (default, medium batching), ECO (high batching, quantized kernels). Tenant requests are mapped to slabs via SLA bucket headers or heuristic admission (recent p95/p99 history).
- Kernel probing: lightweight microbench probes run periodically per model-kernel pair using short synthetic sequences that mimic observed attention density. Probes produce a small performance table (latency per token, throughput per batch size) that is cached on the node and tagged by model-version + attention-density quantile.
- Attention micro-prober: at request arrival, compute a cheap attention-density sketch (approx ratio of non-pad tokens, configured sparse-attn markers) and look up the probe table for kernel hints. If missing, fall back to a conservative kernel and enqueue an async probe job.
- Phase splitting: split prefill and decode into micro-phases aligned with slab choice. E.g., FAST slab prefill uses preemptive KV-cache reservation and smaller decode windows; ECO slab accepts larger prefill windows and defers certain hedged paths.
- Packing & hedging: within BALANCED/ECO slabs use dynamic subbatch packing guided by the probe estimates to maximize GPU utilization while respecting slab latency ceilings. For FAST slab, pack minimally and enable hedging (duplicate to a fast kernel variant on spare capacity).
- Fairness: tenant weights applied at slab allocation time; ensure tenant satisfactions by soft reservations (credits) and a fast fallback path when credit depleted. Implement a slow-start decay to avoid starvation.

Instrumentation & metrics: capture slab assignment counts, slab-specific p50/p95/p99, kernel-probe freshness and hit rate, microbatch packing efficiency, hedging frequency, tenant credit usage, and cost delta per-token. Add synthetic probes dashboard and a per-node probe cache size metric.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature flag guarded prototype: enable slab assignment in a single canary region for a subset of tenants.
2) Collect metrics for two weeks, compare p99 for FAST tenants and overall throughput.
3) Gradually enable kernel probing and hedging.
4) Full rollout after safety window and SRE sign-off.

Docs & artifacts: design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.company/display/RUNTIME/Phase+Slab+Allocator, experiment notebook (Drive): https://drive.redwood.company/drive/folders/phase-slab-experiments, initial PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6124

Acceptance criteria:
- FAST slab p99 reduced by >=20% for targeted tenants versus baseline
- Overall token throughput loss <= 5% in canary region when slab allocator enabled
- Kernel probe hit rate > 70% after 24h of canary traffic
- No tenant starvation incidents during 2-week canary window
